title: Mobility patterns are associated with experienced income segregation in large US cities
authors: Esteban Moro; Dan Calacci; Xiaowen Dong; Alex Pentland
abstract: Abstract Traditional understanding of urban income segregation is largely based on static coarse-grained residential patterns. However, these do not capture the income segregation experience implied by the rich social interactions that happen in places that may relate to individual choices, opportunities, and mobility behavior. Using a large-scale high-resolution mobility data set of 4.5 million mobile phone users and 1.1 million places in 11 large American cities, we show that income segregation experienced in places and by individuals can differ greatly even within close spatial proximity. To further understand these fine-grained income segregation patterns, we introduce a Schelling extension of a well-known mobility model, and show that experienced income segregation is associated with an individual’s tendency to explore new places (place exploration) as well as places with visitors from different income groups (social exploration). Interestingly, while the latter is more strongly associated with demographic characteristics, the former is more strongly associated with mobility behavioral variables. Our results suggest that mobility behavior plays an important role in experienced income segregation of individuals. To measure this form of income segregation, urban researchers should take into account mobility behavior and not only residential patterns.
abstractZh: 对城市收入隔离的传统理解，主要建立在静态、粗粒度的居住模式上。然而，这些模式无法捕捉发生于不同场所的丰富社会互动所蕴含的收入隔离体验，而这些互动可能与个体选择、机会和移动行为有关。本文利用覆盖美国11个大城市450万手机用户和110万个地点的大规模高分辨率移动数据，表明即使空间距离很近，地点和个体实际经历的收入隔离也可能大不相同。为进一步理解这些精细尺度模式，我们在一种知名移动模型中引入谢林式扩展，发现体验收入隔离与个体探索新地点的倾向（地点探索），以及探索有不同收入群体访客的地点的倾向（社会探索）相关。值得注意的是，后者与人口特征的联系更强，而前者与移动行为变量的联系更强。结果表明，移动行为对个体体验的收入隔离具有重要作用。为测量这种收入隔离，城市研究者应同时考虑移动行为，而不只考虑居住模式。
